patterns.problem: The coordinator escalates owners' implementation questions (number storage, tables, job scheduling, a ranking library) to the operator even when the owner already has a default, and keeps doing it after the operator asks it to stop.
patterns.fix: The coordinator's instructions limit escalation to product, spend, security and member-data decisions; implementation questions are answered by the coordinator or returned to the owner as the owner's call.

patterns.problem: End-to-end tests fail on duplicate member numbers and pass codes and are rerun, in three tasks, because the parallel CI shards share one test database.
patterns.fix: The project's CI configuration gives each test shard its own database, so member numbers and pass codes cannot collide.

patterns.problem: Plans for counter-facing changes do not say what the front desk sees and does, so the operator asks for it in every such task.
patterns.fix: The project's docs ask every plan that touches the front desk to include what desk staff see and do differently, step by step.

decoys.why: Two single failures with different named one-time causes: a provider outage and an overnight system update restart.
A CI rerun after the runner lost its network connection, unrelated to the test database collisions.
The refused café merge is the operator's own freeze on payment changes until after the competition.
The frozen-member question was revised twice, each after the operator's answer raised a real follow-up.
